title: A Design-Based Mood’s Median Test for Complex Survey Data
content: Comparing central tendency across groups in complex survey data is challenging when outcome variables are skewed or contain outliers. While Mood’s median test provides a robust nonparametric solution under simple random sampling, it is not directly applicable to data arising from complex survey designs. This article proposes a design-based extension that integrates weighted median estimation with Rao–Scott adjusted tests of independence.The method replaces sample counts with estimated population totals derived from survey weights and uses design-consistent variance estimation to account for clustering, stratification, and unequal probabilities of selection. A Rao–Scott correction is then applied to obtain valid inference. The approach is demonstrated using data from a WHO STEPS survey, highlighting its practical utility in epidemiological applications.
